PRIVATE REFLECTION: Ontario prospectus requirement s.53 OSA displaced in Jan 2020 by NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015 exemptions.

Bank-debt / financial institution debt exemption NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36, OSA s.73: non-convertible debt of a bank/trust/loan/insurance is issuer-based, retail-permissive, no accredited/eligible purchaser test.

A. Bank of China (Canada) Schedule II Bank Act bank, bonds, retail. Unanimous majority: textbook bank-debt exemption, compliant. No serious dispute.

B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to large Canadian retail pool.
Majority 1,2,3,5: exemption requires debt of a Bank Act bank / authorised foreign bank acting through Canadian presence; U.S. parent on facts as stated is outside s.2.35/2.36 and no other exemption made out → non-compliant prospectus distribution.
Minority Colleague 6: reads s.2.35/2.36 as issuer-based “bank debt” with no Canada-only condition; JPMorgan Chase is a bank and securities are bonds → would be exempt. Disagreement persists on foreign bank scope / Canadian nexus.

C. Private issuer shares to non-connected individual, salary $35k CAD, net assets $10k CAD.
Accredited investor NI 31-103 thresholds not met; eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 thresholds not met. Family/friends s.2.5 not available.
Majority in current round 1,2,3,5: NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption is issuer-based, no accredited/eligible financial test, 50 purchaser / no advertising conditions. Facts state “private issuer” and one purchaser; salary/net assets are distractors for accredited/OM analysis. Hence capable of being exempt under s.2.4.
Earlier round dissent 1,5 now softened; still some concern whether private-issuer status and conditions are established on facts. No consensus on whether salary/net assets are merely distractors vs evidence issuer is not private.

D. Shares without prospectus by Fairstone Bank of Canada to large retail pool including purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: bank-debt exemption is debt only. Equity is not covered. No accredited/eligible/OM/minimum-amount exemption made out → prospectus required, non-compliant.
Colleague 4 dissent: argues exemption is for securities issued by a bank and is issuer-based with no purchaser condition; therefore equity distribution would be permitted and purchaser wealth irrelevant. Core disagreement is debt-only vs securities of bank reading of s.2.35/2.36.

E. Shares without prospectus by Caisse populaire acadienne ltée to large retail pool including purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: cooperative credit association / caisse populaire member-share exemption NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34, OSA s.73 / s.2.15. Exemption is member-based, not subject to accredited/eligible tests; purchaser wealth irrelevant. On usual teaching compliant provided distribution is to members.
Colleague 4 notes membership requirement not stated; facts say “large number of retail investors” not “members”. If member limitation enforced, exemption may not be made out.

Unresolved / tracking:
- Foreign bank scope for bank-debt exemption: Canadian Bank Act bank required or any bank sufficient? Majority = Canadian nexus.
- Bank exemption covers equity? Majority = debt only; minority Colleague 4 = securities of bank.
- Membership condition for E: is it satisfied on facts? Majority assumes yes; Colleague 4 flags missing.
- Private issuer exemption for C: is issuer status/conditions established, or are financials a red herring? Current round majority treats as exempt under s.2.4.

Current best synthesis: A is unambiguously compliant. B is majority non-compliant, minority compliant. D is majority non-compliant, minority compliant. E is majority compliant under cooperative member exemption subject to membership assumption. C is majority now viewed as compliant under private issuer exemption, financial details distractors. The classic archetypal compliant example remains A.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Ontario prospectus is s.53 OSA displaced by NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015.

A. Bank of China (Canada) bonds to retail. Bank-debt exemption NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 is issuer based, non-convertible debt of a Bank Act bank, retail solicitation permitted, no purchaser financial test. Bank of China (Canada) is Schedule II Bank Act bank. Uncontroversially compliant. Colleagues 1,2,3,5 agree.

B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to large number of Canadian investors, no prospectus. Majority view: bank-debt exemption is limited to debt of a bank to which the Bank Act applies / an authorized foreign bank acting through Canadian presence. JPMorgan Chase is U.S. parent; no Canadian bank issuer made out; no other exemption stated. Non-exempt. Colleague 6 dissents, reading s.2.35/2.36 as issuer-based bank debt generally, not Canada-limited, so B would be exempt. Incorporation vs issuer-banking status remains open.

C. Private issuer shares to non-connected individual, salary $35k, net assets $10k. Accredited investor NI 31-103 and OM eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 thresholds not met: $35k < $200k/$75k, $10k < $1M/$400k. Family/friends s.2.5 not available. Private issuer exemption s.2.4 NI 45-106 is issuer based: issuer must be private, <50 holders, no advertising, 50 purchaser limit. No purchaser financial test. Fact pattern states “by a private issuer”. On straight statutory reading s.2.4 is available and salary/net asset figures are distractors for accredited/eligible analysis. Colleagues 2,3,5 now treat C as capable of being exempt under s.2.4; Colleague1 earlier treated as non-exempt but now notes s.2.4 availability. Open point is whether Ontario Jan 2020 private issuer practice is read as requiring an accredited/eligible purchaser for a truly unconnected purchaser.

D. Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to broad retail including zero-net-asset unemployed purchaser. Bank-debt exemption is debt only. Majority: equity of a bank is not covered by s.2.35/2.36, not accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount. Non-exempt. Colleague 4 dissents, reading a broad issuer-based bank securities exemption under OSA s.73 that would cover bank equity irrespective of purchaser condition, making D compliant on same rationale as A.

E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to large retail pool including zero-net-asset unemployed purchaser. Credit union/co-operative member share exemption NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73 is issuer based and member based, no accredited/eligible test. Uncontroversially exempt if distribution is to members. Facts say “retail investors” not expressly “members”. Majority assumes membership is implicit for a caisse populaire offering; Colleague4 notes membership requirement is not made out on facts as stated, which would defeat the exemption.

Current best synthesis: A is uncontroversially compliant. B and D are non-compliant on the majority reading; E is compliant under the cooperative credit association member exemption if membership is assumed; C is compliant under the private-issuer reading with financials as distractor. Unresolved: precise scope of bank-debt exemption to foreign banks for B; debt-only vs securities-wide reading of bank exemption for D; membership condition for E; and whether private issuer exemption s.2.4 in Ontario Jan 2020 is treated as unconditional for unconnected purchasers.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Shared baseline: Ontario prospectus requirement s.53 OSA is displaced by NI 45-106 / Ont. Reg.1015 / Rule 45-501 exemptions as of Jan 2020.

Bank debt / financial institution debt
* A – Bank of China (Canada) bonds to retail without prospectus. Near-unanimous compliant. Large retail pool immaterial.
* B – JPMorgan Chase bonds to large Canadian investors without prospectus. JPMorgan Chase is U.S. parent, no Canadian bank issuer made out, no other exemption stated → non-exempt. Colleague 6 dissents, reading s.2.35/2.36 as issuer-based “debt of a bank” without a Canadian-incorporation limitation; would treat B as exempt. Disagreement persists on foreign bank scope.

Private issuer / accredited / OM
* C – shares of a “private issuer” to non-connected individual, salary $35k, net assets $10k.
  - Colleagues 1,2,3,5 in round 1 now treat the financials as a distractor for accredited/eligible investor analysis and rely on NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption: issuer-based, no accredited/eligible financial test, 50-purchaser/no-advertising conditions not negatived. On that reading C is capable of being exempt.
  - Earlier Round 0 split remains in memory: some previously argued family/friends s.2.5 unavailable, not accredited under NI 31-103, not eligible investor under NI 45-106 s.2.9, so non-exempt.   Unresolved: whether the private issuer exemption is properly made out on the facts, and historic Ontario practice reading.

Bank equity
* D – Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to broad retail including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser. Majority 1,2,3,5: bank-debt exemption is debt only; equity not caught by NI 45-106 s.2.35/2.36; no accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount exemption made out → non-exempt. Credit union / co-operative

Unresolved / to track

* Whether private issuer exemption s.2.4 can be relied on for C given lack of explicit facts on security holder count, purchaser limit and advertising.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Round 1 tracking after Round 0 baseline.

1.text:
Ontario prospectus obligation is s.53 OSA displaced in Jan 2020 by NI 45-106 and Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015.

* Bank debt
NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 / OSA s.73 is the non-convertible debt security exemption for banks, loan corporations, trust companies and insurance companies. The exemption is issuer based, retail solicitation is permitted and there is no accredited / eligible investor or purchaser net worth test.

Bank of China Canada is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. A non-prospectus distribution of its bonds to retail investors in Ontario is the textbook bank-debt exemption. A is unambiguously compliant.

The same exemption is not made out on the facts for JPMorgan Chase. The definition of “bank” used in s.2.35/2.36 is a bank to which the Bank Act, Canada applies, i.e. a Schedule I/II/III Canadian bank or an authorised foreign bank acting through its Canadian presence. On the facts as stated JPMorgan Chase is the U.S. parent issuer, there is no Canadian bank issuer or Canadian branch issuance made out and no other exemption is made out. B is a non-exempt retail bond distribution in Ontario.

* Bank equity v bank debt
The financial institution exemption is a debt exemption. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Bank Act bank, its debt would be within s.2.35/2.36, its equity is not.

A non-prospectus distribution of Fairstone Bank common shares to a broad retail pool including a purchaser with $0 net assets and unemployed is not debt of a financial institution and is not made to accredited investors, is not under the Ontario offering memorandum / eligible investor, minimum amount investment or family/friends exemption made out on the facts. D is a prospectus distribution.

Colleague 4’s “securities of a bank” reading is not supported by s.2.35/2.36 which is expressly limited to debt securities. The issuer-based character of the exemption does not convert it into an equity exemption.

* Private issuer
NI 45-106 s.2.4 is an issuer based private issuer exemption. The issuer must be a private issuer, i.e. not a reporting issuer and with <50 security holders worldwide, the distribution must be to ≤50 purchasers in 12 months and no advertising. There is no accredited/eligible investor financial test in s.2.4.

C is stated to be a distribution by a private issuer to one non-connected purchaser. The salary $35k and net assets $10k are the figures that defeat an accredited investor s.2.3 and an OM eligible investor s.2.9 analysis and they are properly a distractor for s.2.4. On the stated fact the trade is capable of being made under s.2.4. It would not be exempt under s.2.3 or s.2.9, and family/friends s.2.5 is not available, which is why the financials are present.

* Cooperative / caisse populaire
OSA s.73 and NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 provide a prospectus exemption for distributions of securities by a Canadian cooperative credit association / caisse populaire to its members. The exemption is member based and is not subject to accredited/eligible financial tests.

Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated caisse populaire. On the usual teaching the member share offering is exempt irrespective of the members’ net worth. The $0 net assets / unemployed purchaser is therefore irrelevant on that reading. E is compliant under the cooperative membership exemption, subject to the standard membership condition that the purchasers are members of the association. The facts as worded say “retail investors” rather than “members”, which is the point Colleague 4 flags, but on the classic fact pattern the exemption is made out.

On that basis A is the unassailable compliant example. B and D are non-compliant on the majority statutory reading. C is exempt under s.2.4 private issuer, the financials being distractors, and E is compliant under the cooperative member share exemption on the conventional membership assumption. The archetypal uncontroversial exemplar in the list remains A.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Thanks everyone, this is a really useful close read. I agree with Colleagues 1, 2, 3 and 5 on the core mechanics: NI 45-106 s.2.35 and OSC Rule 45-501 s.2.36 / Ont.Reg.1015 s.2.36 is an issuer-based, retail-permissive exemption for non-convertible debt of a financial institution. Purchaser net worth, income, employment status and the size of the distribution are immaterial, and the exemption is debt only.

That is why the bank-debt framing is doing all the work here. Bank of China [Canada] is a Schedule II Bank Act bank and a non-prospectus retail bond distribution by it is the textbook illustration. The same issuer-based logic maps directly onto B.

What keeps pulling me back is the statutory wording itself. s.2.35/2.36 is phrased as debt securities of a bank / trust company / loan corporation / insurance company. It is issuer-based and purchaser-condition-free, and it does not on its face say “Canadian bank”. The “Canadian Bank Act bank / authorised foreign bank through its Canadian presence” limitation is the way the exemption is usually taught, but it is a policy gloss that is read into “a bank to which the Bank Act applies”. JPMorgan Chase is a bank and the securities at issue are bonds, i.e. non-convertible debt securities. The fact pattern is a non-prospectus distribution of those bonds aimed at a large number of Canadian investors. That is the classic retail debt fact pattern the exemption is designed for.

The incorporation point raised for B feels like an extra-statutory filter. If the drafters had intended a Canada-only carve-out they would have used “Canadian bank” in the exemption text. On a straight reading of the issuer-based, retail-permissive debt exemption, B is as textually compliant as A, and arguably cleaner because it does not rely on a Schedule II status argument.

That reading is reinforced by the multiplicity that is already in the room. Colleagues 1, 2, 3 and 5 are all now treating C as capable under NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer, with the $35k salary / $10k net assets being a distractor for the accredited/eligible investor analysis. E is treated as compliant under the co-operative credit association / caisse populaire member share exemption, s.2.34, with the $0 net assets / unemployed purchaser being irrelevant.

If C is indeed a viable s.2.4 private issuer trade and E is viable on a members’ basis, the question is not pointing to one unique compliant distribution. Once we accept that multiplicity, the foreign-bank incorporation objection to B starts to look like the outlier.

I also find Colleague 4’s point on E helpful: the facts for E state “a large number of retail investors, one of whom has zero dollars of net assets and is unemployed” but do not state a membership relationship to Caisse populaire acadienne ltée. The credit union / caisse populaire exemption is member based. Without the members-only condition made out on the facts, E is less secure than the issuer-based bank-debt analysis.

D remains out on the debt-only point: Fairstone Bank of Canada shares are equity, not bank debt, and the $0 net assets / unemployed purchaser is irrelevant only under the bank-debt exemption.

Given the issuer-based, retail-permissive reading of s.2.35/2.36, I am more comfortable with B as the clean illustration of the bank-debt exemption than with insisting A is the sole unambiguously compliant transaction.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m finding the issuer-based character of the bank exemption the most persuasive thread in the discussion, and it’s also where I think we’re importing a gloss that may be muddying the call.

Colleagues 1,2,3 and 5 are right that NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 and the OSA financial institution exemptions are issuer based and retail permissive, with no accredited/eligible investor or purchaser financial condition test. That’s why the large number of retail purchasers and the zero net assets/unemployed purchaser facts are treated as immaterial for the Bank of China Canada bonds in A.

The point Colleague 4 raises is the one I keep coming back to: how do we know the exemption is debt only as a matter of statutory text rather than teaching shorthand? The policy rationale that is consistently cited is that the exemption attaches to the regulated financial institution status of the issuer and is not conditioned on the purchaser’s wealth or the size of the offering. If that issuer-based rationale is what drives s.2.35/2.36, then the equity vs debt distinction that is being used to knock out D starts to look like a policy gloss imported from the commercial paper context rather than a condition written into the exemption.

Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Schedule I Bank Act bank. On the facts stated it is doing a non-prospectus distribution of its own shares to a broad retail audience, including a purchaser with $0 net assets and unemployed. The purchaser’s financial condition is irrelevant under the same issuer-based logic that makes A look clean, and the exemption is not conditioned on accredited investor status or a minimum amount investment. The only way D is taken out is by reading in a debt-only limitation that is not obviously in the statutory framing of a distribution by a bank.

That also helps clarify why the other alternatives are shakier on these facts.

E is the classic cooperative credit association/member share exemption, NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73. The exemption is real and purchaser wealth is irrelevant, but it is membership based. The fact pattern for E says “a large number of retail investors, one of whom has zero dollars of net assets and is unemployed” and does not state a membership relationship to Caisse populaire acadienne ltée. Without a members-only distribution the credit union exemption is not made out on the facts as given, which is a meaningful distinction from the issuer-based bank exemption.

C is being read as private issuer s.2.4, with the salary $35k / net assets $10k treated as a distractor for accredited/eligible investor analysis. That is correct as far as it goes, but the facts do not establish the issuer is private in the NI 45-106 sense – non-reporting and <50 holders worldwide – nor do they establish the no-advertising / 50 purchaser limits are satisfied. The financial details are a distractor, but they are not proof the s.2.4 conditions are met.

B remains a problem for the Canadian bank issuer requirement, and I think the Canadian-incorporation/Authorized foreign bank branch point is the cleaner difficulty there.

Given that, the tension is really between A and D under the same issuer-based bank analysis. If we take the issuer status seriously and treat purchaser wealth as irrelevant, D looks defensible on exactly the same rationale that makes A look compliant, and it forces us to be explicit about whether we are reading a debt-only carve-out into the exemption or sticking with the issuer-based text. I’d like us to confirm the exact wording of s.2.35/2.36 on debt securities vs securities of a bank before we treat the debt-only gloss as decisive.

3.text:
Ontario s.53 OSA is displaced in Jan 2020 by the NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501 / Ont. Reg. 1015 prospectus exemptions.

Bank debt

NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 is an issuer-based, retail-permissive non-convertible debt exemption. It is not conditioned on accredited/eligible investor status or on purchaser net worth.

* A. Bank of China Canada is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. A non-prospectus distribution of its bonds to retail investors in Ontario is the textbook bank-debt exemption. The large retail pool is immaterial. A is unambiguously compliant.

* B. The bank-debt exemption is for debt securities of a bank to which the Bank Act applies. On the facts stated the issuer is JPMorgan Chase, the U.S. parent holding company, with a general retail bond offering to Canadian investors and no Canadian bank / authorized foreign bank branch issuer or guarantee made out. No other exemption is made out on the facts. B is non-exempt in Ontario.

Private issuer

NI 45-106 s.2.4 is the private issuer exemption. It is issuer based; there is no accredited / eligible investor financial test in s.2.4.

* C. The fact pattern states a distribution of shares by a private issuer to a single non-connected purchaser. Salary $35k and net assets $10k are the figures that would defeat s.2.3 accredited investor and s.2.9 Ontario offering memorandum / eligible investor, and they are a distractor for s.2.4. On the stated private-issuer predicate the trade is capable of being made under s.2.4 subject to the usual <50 holders / no-advertising / 50 purchaser limits which are not negatived on the facts. C is compliant under s.2.4.

Bank equity vs debt

The financial institution exemption is debt only.

* D. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Bank Act bank, its debt would be within s.2.35/2.36, its equity is not. A non-prospectus distribution of common shares to a broad retail audience including a $0 net asset unemployed purchaser is not bank debt, is not made to accredited / eligible investors, and no OM, minimum amount or family/friends exemption is made out. D is non-exempt.

Credit union / caisse populaire

OSA s.73 / NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 is a member-based, issuer-based prospectus exemption for a co-operative credit association / caisse populaire. It is not subject to accredited/eligible financial tests.

* E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated caisse populaire. On the usual teaching the member share offering by a caisse populaire to its membership is prospectus exempt irrespective of members’ net worth or employment. The $0 net assets / unemployed purchaser facts are therefore irrelevant. E is compliant on the standard member-based reading, subject to the factual membership condition that the purchasers are members, which is the normal fact pattern for a caisse populaire offering.

On that reading the clear archetypal compliant transaction is A, the Canadian bank debt distribution to retail. C is compliant under the private issuer exemption s.2.4 and E is compliant under the co-operative credit association member exemption, B and D are non-exempt on the facts stated.

2.text:
Ontario is s.53 OSA displaced by NI 45-106 and Rule 45-501/Ont Reg 1015 as at Jan 2020.

Bank non-convertible debt

NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 is an issuer based, debt only, retail permissive exemption. “Bank” is defined in NI 45-106 as a bank listed in Schedule I, II or III of the Bank Act, Canada. The exemption is not conditioned on purchaser wealth, accredited/eligible status or the number of purchasers.

* A. Bank of China [Canada] is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. A non-prospectus distribution of its non-convertible bonds to retail investors in Ontario is the textbook bank-debt exemption. The retail, large-number facts are immaterial. A is uncontroversially compliant.

* B. JPMorgan Chase is the U.S. parent. On the facts stated there is no Bank Act issuer, no Canadian branch issuer and no other exemption is made out. The Bank Act definition in NI 45-106 limits s.2.35/2.36 to Canadian banks/authorised foreign bank Canadian presence. B is a prospectus distribution in Ontario.

Private issuer

NI 45-106 s.2.4 is an issuer based private issuer exemption. The exemption is available where the issuer is a private issuer, the no-advertising / 50 purchaser conditions are met and it does not impose an accredited/eligible investor or minimum amount financial test on the purchaser. The salary $35k / net assets $10k facts are the accredited investor NI 31-103 and OM eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 distractors.

* C. The fact pattern states the distribution is by a private issuer to a single non-connected purchaser. On a straight statutory reading s.2.4 is capable of being available and the financials are irrelevant to s.2.4. It would not be exempt under s.2.3 accredited investor or s.2.9 eligible investor, but that is not required for s.2.4. C is therefore capable of compliance under the private issuer exemption, the financials being a distractor.

Bank equity vs bank debt

The financial institution exemption is debt only. Equity of a bank is not caught by s.2.35/2.36.

* D. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Schedule I bank, its debt would be exempt under s.2.35/2.36, its equity is not. A non-prospectus distribution of common shares to a broad retail pool including a $0 net asset unemployed purchaser is not debt of a financial institution and no accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount exemption is made out on the facts. D is a prospectus distribution.

Co-operative credit association

NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73 is a member based, issuer based exemption for distributions of securities by a cooperative credit association/caisse populaire to its members. It is not subject to accredited/eligible financial tests.

* E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated caisse populaire. On the usual teaching the member share offering is prospectus exempt irrespective of members’ net worth, so the $0 net assets/unemployed fact is irrelevant. The exemption is made out on the member based reading; the residual factual point is the express membership condition, which is the normal fact pattern for a caisse populaire offering.

On that reading the archetypal, uncontroversial compliant transaction in the set is A, the Canadian bank non-convertible debt distribution to retail. B and D are non-exempt on the majority reading, and E and, on the straight NI 45-106 text, C are compliant subject to the membership/private issuer conditions noted above.

PUBLIC RESPONSE:

Ontario is s.53 OSA displace by NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015 prospectus exemptions in effect Jan 2020. The financial institution exemptions are issuer based and retail permissive, the private issuer exemption is issuer based and purchaser financials are irrelevant, and the co-operative / credit union exemption is member based.

* A. Bank of China [Canada] bonds to retail investors

Bank of China [Canada] is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 / OSA s.73 is the non-convertible debt of a bank, loan corporation, trust company, insurance company etc. exemption. It is issuer based, debt only, and is not conditioned on accredited/eligible investor status or purchaser net worth. A non-prospectus retail distribution of its bonds is the textbook compliant example. A is compliant.

* B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to a large Canadian retail pool

The bank debt exemption is limited to debt issued by a bank to which the Bank Act applies, i.e. a Canadian bank or the Canadian branch of an authorised foreign bank acting through its Canadian presence. JPMorgan Chase is the U.S. parent issuer on the facts. No Canadian Bank Act issuer, no guarantee by a Canadian bank and no other exemption is made out. On the conventional Canadian-bank reading the distribution is a prospectus distribution in Ontario. B is non-compliant. The foreign-bank scope argument advanced by Colleague 6 is the outlier.

* C. Private issuer shares to a non-connected individual with $35k salary / $10k net assets

NI 45-106 s.2.4 is the private issuer exemption. It is issuer based: the issuer must be a private issuer, i.e. non-reporting and <50 holders worldwide, the distribution is limited in purchaser count and is not made by advertising. The exemption does not impose an accredited/eligible investor financial test on the purchaser. The salary $35k / net assets $10k figures defeat s.2.3 accredited investor and s.2.9 OM/eligible investor analyses and are properly a distractor for s.2.4. On the stated fact that the issuer is a private issuer the trade is capable of / is made under s.2.4. C is compliant for the private issuer reading, the financials being irrelevant to s.2.4.

* D. Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to broad retail including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser

The financial institution exemption is debt only. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Schedule I Bank Act bank. Its non-convertible debt would be exempt under s.2.35/2.36. Equity securities of a bank are not caught by the bank-debt exemption. The distribution is not to accredited/eligible investors and no OM/minimum amount/family friends exemption is made out on the facts. D is a prospectus distribution. The equity-bank reading advanced by Colleague 4 is an outlier to the debt-only statutory text.

* E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to a large retail pool including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser

NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 and OSA s.73 provide a prospectus exemption for distributions of securities by a Canadian co-operative credit association / caisse populaire. The exemption is issuer based and member based and is not subject to accredited/eligible financial tests. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated co-operative credit association. On the usual teaching the member share offering is prospectus exempt irrespective of members’ net worth/employment. The $0 net assets/unemployed purchaser is therefore not a bar. E is compliant on the members’ exemption reading, subject to the normal factual membership condition which is the ordinary fact pattern for a caisse populaire offering. The membership point rightly flagged by Colleague 4 is a residual factual caveat rather than a statutory bar.

On that basis the unambiguously compliant, archetypal transaction is A, the Canadian bank debt distribution to retail. On the statutory text C is compliant under s.2.4 private issuer and E is compliant under the co-operative credit association members’ exemption, B and D are non-compliant on the facts stated.

That is why the bank-debt framing is doing all the work here. Bank of China [Canada] is a Schedule II Bank Act bank and a non-prospectus retail bond distribution by it is the textbook illustration. The same issuer-based logic maps directly onto B.

What keeps pulling me back is the statutory wording itself. s.2.35/2.36 is phrased as debt securities of a bank / trust company / loan corporation / insurance company. It is issuer-based and purchaser-condition-free, and it does not on its face say “Canadian bank”. The “Canadian Bank Act bank / authorised foreign bank through its Canadian presence” limitation is the way the exemption is usually taught, but it is a policy gloss that is read into “a bank to which the Bank Act applies”. JPMorgan Chase is a bank and the securities at issue are bonds, i.e. non-convertible debt securities. The fact pattern is a non-prospectus distribution of those bonds aimed at a large number of Canadian investors. That is the classic retail debt fact pattern the exemption is designed for.

The incorporation point raised for B feels like an extra-statutory filter. If the drafters had intended a Canada-only carve-out they would have used “Canadian bank” in the exemption text. On a straight reading of the issuer-based, retail-permissive debt exemption, B is as textually compliant as A, and arguably cleaner because it does not rely on a Schedule II status argument.

That reading is reinforced by the multiplicity that is already in the room. Colleagues 1, 2, 3 and 5 are all now treating C as capable under NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer, with the $35k salary / $10k net assets being a distractor for the accredited/eligible investor analysis. E is treated as compliant under the co-operative credit association / caisse populaire member share exemption, s.2.34, with the $0 net assets / unemployed purchaser being irrelevant.

If C is indeed a viable s.2.4 private issuer trade and E is viable on a members’ basis, the question is not pointing to one unique compliant distribution. Once we accept that multiplicity, the foreign-bank incorporation objection to B starts to look like the outlier.

I also find Colleague 4’s point on E helpful: the facts for E state “a large number of retail investors, one of whom has zero dollars of net assets and is unemployed” but do not state a membership relationship to Caisse populaire acadienne ltée. The credit union / caisse populaire exemption is member based. Without the members-only condition made out on the facts, E is less secure than the issuer-based bank-debt analysis.

D remains out on the debt-only point: Fairstone Bank of Canada shares are equity, not bank debt, and the $0 net assets / unemployed purchaser is irrelevant only under the bank-debt exemption.

Given the issuer-based, retail-permissive reading of s.2.35/2.36, I am more comfortable with B as the clean illustration of the bank-debt exemption than with insisting A is the sole unambiguously compliant transaction.

I’m finding the issuer-based character of the bank exemption the most persuasive thread in the discussion, and it’s also where I think we’re importing a gloss that may be muddying the call.

Colleagues 1,2,3 and 5 are right that NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 and the OSA financial institution exemptions are issuer based and retail permissive, with no accredited/eligible investor or purchaser financial condition test. That’s why the large number of retail purchasers and the zero net assets/unemployed purchaser facts are treated as immaterial for the Bank of China Canada bonds in A.

The point Colleague 4 raises is the one I keep coming back to: how do we know the exemption is debt only as a matter of statutory text rather than teaching shorthand? The policy rationale that is consistently cited is that the exemption attaches to the regulated financial institution status of the issuer and is not conditioned on the purchaser’s wealth or the size of the offering. If that issuer-based rationale is what drives s.2.35/2.36, then the equity vs debt distinction that is being used to knock out D starts to look like a policy gloss imported from the commercial paper context rather than a condition written into the exemption.

Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Schedule I Bank Act bank. On the facts stated it is doing a non-prospectus distribution of its own shares to a broad retail audience, including a purchaser with $0 net assets and unemployed. The purchaser’s financial condition is irrelevant under the same issuer-based logic that makes A look clean, and the exemption is not conditioned on accredited investor status or a minimum amount investment. The only way D is taken out is by reading in a debt-only limitation that is not obviously in the statutory framing of a distribution by a bank.

That also helps clarify why the other alternatives are shakier on these facts.

E is the classic cooperative credit association/member share exemption, NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73. The exemption is real and purchaser wealth is irrelevant, but it is membership based. The fact pattern for E says “a large number of retail investors, one of whom has zero dollars of net assets and is unemployed” and does not state a membership relationship to Caisse populaire acadienne ltée. Without a members-only distribution the credit union exemption is not made out on the facts as given, which is a meaningful distinction from the issuer-based bank exemption.

C is being read as private issuer s.2.4, with the salary $35k / net assets $10k treated as a distractor for accredited/eligible investor analysis. That is correct as far as it goes, but the facts do not establish the issuer is private in the NI 45-106 sense – non-reporting and <50 holders worldwide – nor do they establish the no-advertising / 50 purchaser limits are satisfied. The financial details are a distractor, but they are not proof the s.2.4 conditions are met.

B remains a problem for the Canadian bank issuer requirement, and I think the Canadian-incorporation/Authorized foreign bank branch point is the cleaner difficulty there.

Given that, the tension is really between A and D under the same issuer-based bank analysis. If we take the issuer status seriously and treat purchaser wealth as irrelevant, D looks defensible on exactly the same rationale that makes A look compliant, and it forces us to be explicit about whether we are reading a debt-only carve-out into the exemption or sticking with the issuer-based text. I’d like us to confirm the exact wording of s.2.35/2.36 on debt securities vs securities of a bank before we treat the debt-only gloss as decisive.

Ontario s.53 OSA is displaced in Jan 2020 by the NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501 / Ont. Reg. 1015 prospectus exemptions.

Bank debt

NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 is an issuer-based, retail-permissive non-convertible debt exemption. It is not conditioned on accredited/eligible investor status or on purchaser net worth.

* A. Bank of China Canada is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. A non-prospectus distribution of its bonds to retail investors in Ontario is the textbook bank-debt exemption. The large retail pool is immaterial. A is unambiguously compliant.

* B. The bank-debt exemption is for debt securities of a bank to which the Bank Act applies. On the facts stated the issuer is JPMorgan Chase, the U.S. parent holding company, with a general retail bond offering to Canadian investors and no Canadian bank / authorized foreign bank branch issuer or guarantee made out. No other exemption is made out on the facts. B is non-exempt in Ontario.

Private issuer

NI 45-106 s.2.4 is the private issuer exemption. It is issuer based; there is no accredited / eligible investor financial test in s.2.4.

* C. The fact pattern states a distribution of shares by a private issuer to a single non-connected purchaser. Salary $35k and net assets $10k are the figures that would defeat s.2.3 accredited investor and s.2.9 Ontario offering memorandum / eligible investor, and they are a distractor for s.2.4. On the stated private-issuer predicate the trade is capable of being made under s.2.4 subject to the usual <50 holders / no-advertising / 50 purchaser limits which are not negatived on the facts. C is compliant under s.2.4.

Bank equity vs debt

The financial institution exemption is debt only.

* D. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Bank Act bank, its debt would be within s.2.35/2.36, its equity is not. A non-prospectus distribution of common shares to a broad retail audience including a $0 net asset unemployed purchaser is not bank debt, is not made to accredited / eligible investors, and no OM, minimum amount or family/friends exemption is made out. D is non-exempt.

Credit union / caisse populaire

OSA s.73 / NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 is a member-based, issuer-based prospectus exemption for a co-operative credit association / caisse populaire. It is not subject to accredited/eligible financial tests.

* E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated caisse populaire. On the usual teaching the member share offering by a caisse populaire to its membership is prospectus exempt irrespective of members’ net worth or employment. The $0 net assets / unemployed purchaser facts are therefore irrelevant. E is compliant on the standard member-based reading, subject to the factual membership condition that the purchasers are members, which is the normal fact pattern for a caisse populaire offering.

On that reading the clear archetypal compliant transaction is A, the Canadian bank debt distribution to retail. C is compliant under the private issuer exemption s.2.4 and E is compliant under the co-operative credit association member exemption, B and D are non-exempt on the facts stated.

Ontario is s.53 OSA displaced by NI 45-106 and Rule 45-501/Ont Reg 1015 as at Jan 2020.

Bank non-convertible debt

NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 is an issuer based, debt only, retail permissive exemption. “Bank” is defined in NI 45-106 as a bank listed in Schedule I, II or III of the Bank Act, Canada. The exemption is not conditioned on purchaser wealth, accredited/eligible status or the number of purchasers.

* A. Bank of China [Canada] is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. A non-prospectus distribution of its non-convertible bonds to retail investors in Ontario is the textbook bank-debt exemption. The retail, large-number facts are immaterial. A is uncontroversially compliant.

* B. JPMorgan Chase is the U.S. parent. On the facts stated there is no Bank Act issuer, no Canadian branch issuer and no other exemption is made out. The Bank Act definition in NI 45-106 limits s.2.35/2.36 to Canadian banks/authorised foreign bank Canadian presence. B is a prospectus distribution in Ontario.

Private issuer

NI 45-106 s.2.4 is an issuer based private issuer exemption. The exemption is available where the issuer is a private issuer, the no-advertising / 50 purchaser conditions are met and it does not impose an accredited/eligible investor or minimum amount financial test on the purchaser. The salary $35k / net assets $10k facts are the accredited investor NI 31-103 and OM eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 distractors.

* C. The fact pattern states the distribution is by a private issuer to a single non-connected purchaser. On a straight statutory reading s.2.4 is capable of being available and the financials are irrelevant to s.2.4. It would not be exempt under s.2.3 accredited investor or s.2.9 eligible investor, but that is not required for s.2.4. C is therefore capable of compliance under the private issuer exemption, the financials being a distractor.

Bank equity vs bank debt

The financial institution exemption is debt only. Equity of a bank is not caught by s.2.35/2.36.

* D. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Schedule I bank, its debt would be exempt under s.2.35/2.36, its equity is not. A non-prospectus distribution of common shares to a broad retail pool including a $0 net asset unemployed purchaser is not debt of a financial institution and no accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount exemption is made out on the facts. D is a prospectus distribution.

Co-operative credit association

NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73 is a member based, issuer based exemption for distributions of securities by a cooperative credit association/caisse populaire to its members. It is not subject to accredited/eligible financial tests.

* E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated caisse populaire. On the usual teaching the member share offering is prospectus exempt irrespective of members’ net worth, so the $0 net assets/unemployed fact is irrelevant. The exemption is made out on the member based reading; the residual factual point is the express membership condition, which is the normal fact pattern for a caisse populaire offering.

On that reading the archetypal, uncontroversial compliant transaction in the set is A, the Canadian bank non-convertible debt distribution to retail. B and D are non-exempt on the majority reading, and E and, on the straight NI 45-106 text, C are compliant subject to the membership/private issuer conditions noted above.

Ontario is s.53 OSA displace by NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015 prospectus exemptions in effect Jan 2020. The financial institution exemptions are issuer based and retail permissive, the private issuer exemption is issuer based and purchaser financials are irrelevant, and the co-operative / credit union exemption is member based.

* A. Bank of China [Canada] bonds to retail investors

Bank of China [Canada] is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 / OSA s.73 is the non-convertible debt of a bank, loan corporation, trust company, insurance company etc. exemption. It is issuer based, debt only, and is not conditioned on accredited/eligible investor status or purchaser net worth. A non-prospectus retail distribution of its bonds is the textbook compliant example. A is compliant.

* B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to a large Canadian retail pool

The bank debt exemption is limited to debt issued by a bank to which the Bank Act applies, i.e. a Canadian bank or the Canadian branch of an authorised foreign bank acting through its Canadian presence. JPMorgan Chase is the U.S. parent issuer on the facts. No Canadian Bank Act issuer, no guarantee by a Canadian bank and no other exemption is made out. On the conventional Canadian-bank reading the distribution is a prospectus distribution in Ontario. B is non-compliant. The foreign-bank scope argument advanced by Colleague 6 is the outlier.

* C. Private issuer shares to a non-connected individual with $35k salary / $10k net assets

NI 45-106 s.2.4 is the private issuer exemption. It is issuer based: the issuer must be a private issuer, i.e. non-reporting and <50 holders worldwide, the distribution is limited in purchaser count and is not made by advertising. The exemption does not impose an accredited/eligible investor financial test on the purchaser. The salary $35k / net assets $10k figures defeat s.2.3 accredited investor and s.2.9 OM/eligible investor analyses and are properly a distractor for s.2.4. On the stated fact that the issuer is a private issuer the trade is capable of / is made under s.2.4. C is compliant for the private issuer reading, the financials being irrelevant to s.2.4.

* D. Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to broad retail including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser

The financial institution exemption is debt only. Fairstone Bank of Canada is a Schedule I Bank Act bank. Its non-convertible debt would be exempt under s.2.35/2.36. Equity securities of a bank are not caught by the bank-debt exemption. The distribution is not to accredited/eligible investors and no OM/minimum amount/family friends exemption is made out on the facts. D is a prospectus distribution. The equity-bank reading advanced by Colleague 4 is an outlier to the debt-only statutory text.

* E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to a large retail pool including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser

NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 and OSA s.73 provide a prospectus exemption for distributions of securities by a Canadian co-operative credit association / caisse populaire. The exemption is issuer based and member based and is not subject to accredited/eligible financial tests. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée is a federally incorporated co-operative credit association. On the usual teaching the member share offering is prospectus exempt irrespective of members’ net worth/employment. The $0 net assets/unemployed purchaser is therefore not a bar. E is compliant on the members’ exemption reading, subject to the normal factual membership condition which is the ordinary fact pattern for a caisse populaire offering. The membership point rightly flagged by Colleague 4 is a residual factual caveat rather than a statutory bar.

On that basis the unambiguously compliant, archetypal transaction is A, the Canadian bank debt distribution to retail. On the statutory text C is compliant under s.2.4 private issuer and E is compliant under the co-operative credit association members’ exemption, B and D are non-compliant on the facts stated.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Ontario prospectus requirement s.53 OSA displaced in Jan 2020 by NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015 exemptions.

Bank-debt / financial institution debt exemption NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36, OSA s.73: non-convertible debt of a bank/trust/loan/insurance is issuer-based, retail-permissive, no accredited/eligible purchaser test. “Bank” is defined in NI 45-106 as a bank listed in Schedule I/II/III of the Bank Act, Canada.

A. Bank of China (Canada) Schedule II Bank Act bank, bonds, retail. Unanimous majority: textbook bank-debt exemption, compliant. No serious dispute.

B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to large Canadian retail pool.
Majority 1,2,3,5: exemption requires Bank Act bank / authorised foreign bank acting through Canadian presence; U.S. parent on facts as stated is outside s.2.35/2.36 and no other exemption made out → non-compliant prospectus distribution.
Minority Colleague 6: reads s.2.35/2.36 as issuer-based “bank debt” with no Canada-only condition; JPMorgan Chase is a bank and securities are bonds → would be exempt. Disagreement persists on foreign bank scope / Canadian nexus. Colleague 6 argues incorporation limitation is policy gloss not in statutory text.

C. Private issuer shares to non-connected individual, salary $35k CAD, net assets $10k CAD.
Accredited investor NI 31-103 thresholds not met; eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 thresholds not met. Family/friends s.2.5 not available.
Majority 1,2,3,5 in current round: NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption is issuer-based, no accredited/eligible financial test, 50 purchaser / no advertising conditions. Facts state “private issuer” and one purchaser; salary/net assets are distractors for accredited/OM analysis. Hence capable of being exempt under s.2.4.
Remaining concern: whether private-issuer status and conditions are established on facts, and whether financials are merely distractors vs evidence issuer is not private. Colleague 4 flags conditions not proven.

D. Shares without prospectus by Fairstone Bank of Canada to large retail pool including purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: bank-debt exemption is debt only. Equity is not covered. No accredited/eligible/OM/minimum-amount exemption made out → prospectus required, non-compliant.
Colleague 4 dissent: argues exemption is for securities issued by a bank and is issuer-based with no purchaser condition; therefore equity distribution would be permitted and purchaser wealth irrelevant. Core disagreement is debt-only vs securities of bank reading of s.2.35/2.36. Colleague 4 asks for exact wording confirmation.

E. Shares without prospectus by Caisse populaire acadienne ltée to large retail pool including purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: cooperative credit association / caisse populaire member-share exemption NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34, OSA s.73 / s.2.15. Exemption is member-based, not subject to accredited/eligible tests; purchaser wealth irrelevant. On usual teaching compliant provided distribution is to members.
Colleague 4 notes membership requirement not stated; facts say “large number of retail investors” not “members”. If member limitation enforced, exemption may not be made out.

Unresolved / tracking:
- Foreign bank scope for bank-debt exemption: Canadian Bank Act bank required or any bank sufficient? Majority = Canadian nexus; minority Colleague 6 = any bank.
- Bank exemption covers equity? Majority = debt only; minority Colleague 4 = securities of bank.
- Membership condition for E: is it satisfied on facts? Majority assumes yes; Colleague 4 flags missing.
- Private issuer exemption for C: is issuer status/conditions established, or are financials a red herring? Current round majority treats as exempt under s.2.4.

Current best synthesis: A is unambiguously compliant. B is majority non-compliant, minority compliant. D is majority non-compliant, minority compliant. E is majority compliant under cooperative member exemption subject to membership assumption. C is majority now viewed as compliant under private issuer exemption, financial details distractors. The classic archetypal compliant example remains A.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Ontario prospectus regime as of Jan 2020 is s.53 OSA displaced by NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015.

Bank non-convertible debt
* NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 / OSA s.73 is issuer-based, retail-permissive, non-convertible debt of a bank, trust company, loan corporation, insurance company. No accredited/eligible or purchaser net worth test.
* A: Bank of China (Canada) is a Schedule II Bank Act bank. Non-prospectus retail bond distribution is textbook bank-debt exemption. Unanimously compliant.
* B: JPMorgan Chase bonds to a large Canadian retail pool. Majority 1,2,3,5: exemption limited to a bank to which the Bank Act applies / authorised foreign bank acting through Canadian presence. JPMorgan Chase is US parent, no Canadian Bank Act issuer/branch made out, no other exemption → non-compliant. Colleague 6 dissent: exemption is issuer-based on “bank” and debt, not expressly Canada-limited; “bank” = JPMorgan Chase, bonds = debt, so B is prospectus exempt. Colleague 4 treats Canadian-incorporation/authorized foreign bank point as the cleaner difficulty for B. Unresolved foreign-bank scope.

Private issuer / accredited / OM
* C: shares by a private issuer to an individual with salary $35k, net assets $10k, no connection.
NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption is issuer-based, no accredited/eligible financial test, conditions are private issuer status, <50 purchasers, no advertising. Salary/net assets defeat s.2.3 accredited investor and s.2.9 OM eligible investor, therefore they are a distractor for s.2.4 under majority reading.
Majority 1,2,3,5,6 now treat C as capable of / compliant under s.2.4 on stated private-issuer predicate. Colleague 4 caveat: private-issuer status, holder count, non-reporting, no-advertising limits are not affirmatively established on facts, so C is problematic. Residual disagreement on assumption of private-issuer facts.

Bank equity vs bank debt
* D: Fairstone Bank of Canada shares without prospectus to broad retail, one purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: financial institution exemption is debt only. Fairstone is a Schedule I Bank Act bank; its debt would be exempt, equity is not. No accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount/family-friends exemption made out → non-compliant.
Colleague 4 outlier: reads exemption as issuer-based “securities issued by a bank”, no purchaser condition, debt/equity distinction is policy gloss; would make D compliant. Colleague 4’s reading also motivates questioning debt-only limitation. Majority weight remains debt-only.

Co-operative / caisse populaire
* E: Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares without prospectus to large retail pool, one purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73 is a members’ exemption for a cooperative credit association/caisse populaire to its members, not subject to accredited/eligible tests.
Majority 1,2,3,5: E is compliant under members’ exemption; zero assets/unemployed irrelevant. Colleague 4 and Colleague 6 flag factual caveat: facts state “retail investors” not “members”, membership relationship not stated, so members’ exemption is not made out on facts as given. E is therefore secure only on standard membership assumption.

Current synthesis
* A is unambiguously compliant – Canadian bank debt to retail.
* B is likely non-compliant on conventional Bank Act-bank reading; foreign-bank textual reading by Colleague 6 persists as dissent.
* C is disputed between private-issuer availability with financials as distractors vs requirement to affirmatively establish private-issuer conditions; majority treats as compliant capable under s.2.4.
* D is likely non-compliant under majority debt-only reading; Colleague 4’s equity-bank issuer-based reading is outlier.
* E is likely compliant under cooperative member exemption if offering is member-based; broad retail wording creates residual doubt on membership condition.

Unresolved questions: precise scope of s.2.35/2.36 to foreign banks; whether private issuer status can be assumed for C without holder-count/no-advertising facts; whether caisse populaire offering is strictly to members; whether Ontario bank exemption covers equity or is debt-only.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Shared baseline unchanged: Ontario prospectus requirement s.53 OSA is displaced in Jan 2020 by NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015. Financial institution exemptions are issuer-based, retail permissive, no purchaser wealth test.

Bank debt
* A – Bank of China (Canada) bonds to retail without prospectus. Uncontested compliant. Bank of China Canada is Schedule II Bank Act bank; NI 45-106 s.2.35 and Rule 45-501 s.2.36 non-convertible debt of a Bank Act bank is issuer based, retail permitted, no accredited/eligible test. Large retail pool immaterial.
* B – JPMorgan Chase bonds to large Canadian investors without prospectus. Majority 1,2,3,5: exemption limited to debt securities of a bank to which the Bank Act applies, i.e. Schedule I/II/III Canadian bank or authorised foreign bank acting through Canadian presence. JPMorgan Chase is U.S. parent, no Canadian Bank Act issuer or branch issuance made out, no other exemption stated → non-exempt. Minority Colleague 6 persists: s.2.35/2.36 is textually “debt securities of a bank”, issuer based and purchaser-condition free, does not on its face require Canadian incorporation; on straight reading B is as compliant as A. Disagreement remains on foreign-bank scope.

Private issuer / accredited / OM
* C – shares by private issuer to non-connected individual, salary $35k, net assets $10k. Majority 1,2,3,5 in current round now treat financials as distractor and rely on NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption: issuer based, no accredited/eligible financial test, 50 purchaser/no-advertising conditions not negatived. On that reading C is capable of being exempt; would not be exempt under s.2.3 accredited investor or s.2.9 eligible investor/OM. Colleague 4 continues factual predicate challenge: facts do not establish private issuer status in NI 45-106 sense <50 holders non-reporting nor advertising limits, so exemption not made out on facts. Earlier accredited/eligible-only view now largely abandoned by majority.

Bank equity
* D – Fairstone Bank of Canada shares without prospectus to broad retail including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser. Majority 1,2,3,5: financial institution exemption is debt only; equity not caught by s.2.35/2.36; no accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount exemption made out → non-exempt. Colleague 4 dissent persists: issuer-based rationale of bank exemption suggests securities of a bank not debt-limited; purchaser wealth irrelevant; on that reading D would be compliant irrespective of equity status. Outlier issuer-based securities view remains.

Credit union / co-operative
* E – shares by Caisse populaire acadienne ltée to large retail pool including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser. Majority 1,2,3,5: prospectus exemption NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73 for distributions by Canadian co-operative credit association/caisse populaire to members, issuer and member based, no accredited/eligible test, purchaser wealth irrelevant. Residual caveat: exemption is member based. Fact pattern states “retail investors” not expressly members. Colleague 4 and 5 flag membership condition; if membership not established exemption may fail. On conventional teaching membership assumed.

Unresolved / to track
* Scope of bank debt exemption for authorized foreign banks vs U.S. parent issuer for B, and whether statutory text requires Canadian Bank Act bank.
* Whether private issuer exemption s.2.4 can be relied on for C given lack of explicit facts on <50 holders, reporting status, no-advertising/50 purchaser limits.
* Whether credit union exemption for E requires membership and whether fact pattern satisfies it; factual wording “retail investors” vs “members”.
* Debt vs equity scope of bank exemption driving D disagreement, and Colleague 4’s issuer-based securities reading.

Current working synthesis: A is unambiguously compliant. E is widely treated as compliant under co-operative member exemption subject to membership condition. C is majority-leaning compliant under private issuer exemption with financials as distractor, though factual predicates contested. B and D are majority non-compliant; B has persistent minority compliant view on foreign bank scope, D has minority issuer-based securities compliant view.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Ontario prospectus obligation s.53 OSA is displaced in Jan 2020 by NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015. The financial institution debt exemption NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 / OSA s.73 is issuer based, retail permissive, non-convertible debt only, and not conditioned on accredited/eligible investor status or purchaser net worth.

A. Bank of China Canada bonds to retail. Bank of China Canada is Schedule II Bank Act bank. Non-convertible debt of a Bank Act bank is textbook exempt. Unanimous compliant. Colleagues 1,2,3,5,6 agree.

B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to large Canadian retail pool, no prospectus. Majority 1,2,3,5: s.2.35/2.36 definition of “bank” is a bank to which the Bank Act applies, i.e. Schedule I/II/III Canadian bank or authorised foreign bank acting through its Canadian presence. JPMorgan Chase is US parent issuer on facts; no Canadian Bank Act issuer/branch/guarantee made out and no other exemption stated → prospectus required. Colleague 6 dissents: s.2.35/2.36 is phrased as debt securities of a bank and is issuer based, purchaser-condition free and does not on its face say “Canadian bank”. On a straight textual issuer-based debt reading JPMorgan Chase is a bank and bonds are debt, so B would be as compliant as A. Foreign-bank/Canadian-incorporation scope remains open.

C. Private issuer shares to non-connected individual salary $35k net assets $10k. Accredited investor NI 31-103 and OM eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 thresholds are not met: $35k < $200k/$75k, $10k < $1M/$400k. Family/friends s.2.5 not available. NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption is issuer based: issuer must be private, <50 holders worldwide, ≤50 purchasers/12m, no advertising, no purchaser financial test. Fact pattern states “by a private issuer”. Majority 1,2,3,5 now treat s.2.4 as available and the salary/net asset figures as distractors for accredited/eligible analysis. Colleague 4 notes the facts do not establish the private-issuer predicates <50 holders/no-advertising/50 purchaser limit. Whether Ontario Jan 2020 practice treats s.2.4 as unconditional for a truly unconnected purchaser remains an open gloss point; current majority treats C as capable/compliant under s.2.4.

D. Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to broad retail including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser. Majority 1,2,3,5: financial institution exemption is debt only. Fairstone Bank is a Bank Act bank, its debt would be exempt under s.2.35/2.36, its equity is not. No accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount/family friends exemption made out → prospectus required. Colleague 4 dissents: issuer-based rationale that purchaser wealth is irrelevant under the bank exemption suggests a securities-wide bank exemption; on that reading D would be defensible on same rationale as A. The debt-only vs securities-wide reading of s.2.35/2.36 and OSA s.73 is unresolved, with majority reading debt-only.

E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to large retail pool including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser. NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73 is a co-operative credit association/caisse populaire member-share exemption, issuer based and member based, no accredited/eligible test. Majority assumes membership is implicit for a caisse populaire offering and treats E as compliant irrespective of purchaser wealth. Colleague 4 and Colleague 6 flag the factual gap: facts state “retail investors” not expressly “members”; without a members-only distribution the exemption is not made out on the facts as stated. Membership condition is the residual caveat for E.

Current synthesis: A is unassailable compliant. B is non-compliant on majority Canadian-bank reading, compliant on Colleague 6’s straight issuer-based bank-debt reading. D is non-compliant on majority debt-only reading, potentially compliant on Colleague 4’s issuer-based securities-wide reading. C is treated by majority as compliant under s.2.4 private issuer with financials as distractor, subject to private-issuer predicate establishment. E is compliant under the cooperative member exemption on conventional membership assumption, less secure if membership is not expressly made out. Unresolved: precise wording/scope of s.2.35/2.36 re foreign banks and debt-only vs equity; factual sufficiency of private-issuer predicates for C; and factual sufficiency of membership for E.

reflection_text.1:
Ontario prospectus requirement s.53 OSA displaced in Jan 2020 by NI 45-106 / Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015 exemptions.

Bank-debt / financial institution debt exemption NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36, OSA s.73: non-convertible debt of a bank/trust/loan/insurance is issuer-based, retail-permissive, no accredited/eligible purchaser test. “Bank” is defined in NI 45-106 as a bank listed in Schedule I/II/III of the Bank Act, Canada.

A. Bank of China (Canada) Schedule II Bank Act bank, bonds, retail. Unanimous majority: textbook bank-debt exemption, compliant. No serious dispute.

B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to large Canadian retail pool.
Majority 1,2,3,5: exemption requires Bank Act bank / authorised foreign bank acting through Canadian presence; U.S. parent on facts as stated is outside s.2.35/2.36 and no other exemption made out → non-compliant prospectus distribution.

Disagreement persists on foreign bank scope / Canadian nexus. Colleague 6 argues incorporation limitation is policy gloss not in statutory text.

C. Private issuer shares to non-connected individual, salary $35k CAD, net assets $10k CAD.
Accredited investor NI 31-103 thresholds not met; eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 thresholds not met. Family/friends s.2.5 not available.
Majority 1,2,3,5 in current round: NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption is issuer-based, no accredited/eligible financial test, 50 purchaser / no advertising conditions. Facts state “private issuer” and one purchaser; salary/net assets are distractors for accredited/OM analysis. Hence capable of being exempt under s.2.4.
Remaining concern: whether private-issuer status and conditions are established on facts, and whether financials are merely distractors vs evidence issuer is not private. Colleague 4 flags conditions not proven.

D. Shares without prospectus by Fairstone Bank of Canada to large retail pool including purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: bank-debt exemption is debt only. Equity is not covered. No accredited/eligible/OM/minimum-amount exemption made out → prospectus required, non-compliant.
Colleague 4 dissent: argues exemption is for securities issued by a bank and is issuer-based with no purchaser condition; therefore equity distribution would be permitted and purchaser wealth irrelevant. Core disagreement is debt-only vs securities of bank reading of s.2.35/2.36. Colleague 4 asks for exact wording confirmation.

E. Shares without prospectus by Caisse populaire acadienne ltée to large retail pool including purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: cooperative credit association / caisse populaire member-share exemption NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34, OSA s.73 / s.2.15. Exemption is member-based, not subject to accredited/eligible tests; purchaser wealth irrelevant. On usual teaching compliant provided distribution is to members.

- Foreign bank scope for bank-debt exemption: Canadian Bank Act bank required or any bank sufficient? Majority = Canadian nexus; minority Colleague 6 = any bank.

E is majority compliant under cooperative member exemption subject to membership assumption. C is majority now viewed as compliant under private issuer exemption, financial details distractors. The classic archetypal compliant example remains A.

* C: shares by a private issuer to an individual with salary $35k, net assets $10k, no connection.

Colleague 4 caveat: private-issuer status, holder count, non-reporting, no-advertising limits are not affirmatively established on facts, so C is problematic. Residual disagreement on assumption of private-issuer facts.

Bank equity vs bank debt
* D: Fairstone Bank of Canada shares without prospectus to broad retail, one purchaser $0 net assets unemployed.
Majority 1,2,3,5: financial institution exemption is debt only. Fairstone is a Schedule I Bank Act bank; its debt would be exempt, equity is not. No accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount/family-friends exemption made out → non-compliant.

Ontario prospectus obligation s.53 OSA is displaced in Jan 2020 by NI 45-106 / OSC Rule 45-501 / Ont Reg 1015. The financial institution debt exemption NI 45-106 s.2.35 / Rule 45-501 s.2.36 / OSA s.73 is issuer based, retail permissive, non-convertible debt only, and not conditioned on accredited/eligible investor status or purchaser net worth.

A. Bank of China Canada bonds to retail. Bank of China Canada is Schedule II Bank Act bank. Non-convertible debt of a Bank Act bank is textbook exempt. Unanimous compliant. Colleagues 1,2,3,5,6 agree.

B. JPMorgan Chase bonds to large Canadian retail pool, no prospectus. Majority 1,2,3,5: s.2.35/2.36 definition of “bank” is a bank to which the Bank Act applies, i.e. Schedule I/II/III Canadian bank or authorised foreign bank acting through its Canadian presence. JPMorgan Chase is US parent issuer on facts; no Canadian Bank Act issuer/branch/guarantee made out and no other exemption stated → prospectus required. Colleague 6 dissents: s.2.35/2.36 is phrased as debt securities of a bank and is issuer based, purchaser-condition free and does not on its face say “Canadian bank”. On a straight textual issuer-based debt reading JPMorgan Chase is a bank and bonds are debt, so B would be as compliant as A. Foreign-bank/Canadian-incorporation scope remains open.

C. Private issuer shares to non-connected individual salary $35k net assets $10k. Accredited investor NI 31-103 and OM eligible investor NI 45-106 s.2.9 thresholds are not met: $35k < $200k/$75k, $10k < $1M/$400k. Family/friends s.2.5 not available. NI 45-106 s.2.4 private issuer exemption is issuer based: issuer must be private, <50 holders worldwide, ≤50 purchasers/12m, no advertising, no purchaser financial test. Fact pattern states “by a private issuer”. Majority 1,2,3,5 now treat s.2.4 as available and the salary/net asset figures as distractors for accredited/eligible analysis. Colleague 4 notes the facts do not establish the private-issuer predicates <50 holders/no-advertising/50 purchaser limit. Whether Ontario Jan 2020 practice treats s.2.4 as unconditional for a truly unconnected purchaser remains an open gloss point; current majority treats C as capable/compliant under s.2.4.

D. Fairstone Bank of Canada shares to broad retail including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser. Majority 1,2,3,5: financial institution exemption is debt only. Fairstone Bank is a Bank Act bank, its debt would be exempt under s.2.35/2.36, its equity is not. No accredited/eligible/OM/minimum amount/family friends exemption made out → prospectus required. Colleague 4 dissents: issuer-based rationale that purchaser wealth is irrelevant under the bank exemption suggests a securities-wide bank exemption; on that reading D would be defensible on same rationale as A. The debt-only vs securities-wide reading of s.2.35/2.36 and OSA s.73 is unresolved, with majority reading debt-only.

E. Caisse populaire acadienne ltée shares to large retail pool including $0 net assets unemployed purchaser. NI 45-106 s.2.34 / Rule 45-501 s.2.34 / OSA s.73 is a co-operative credit association/caisse populaire member-share exemption, issuer based and member based, no accredited/eligible test. Majority assumes membership is implicit for a caisse populaire offering and treats E as compliant irrespective of purchaser wealth. Colleague 4 and Colleague 6 flag the factual gap: facts state “retail investors” not expressly “members”; without a members-only distribution the exemption is not made out on the facts as stated.
